title: M5GFX #428: let i2c_stop() reach the pads of an LP I2C port (code-level review)

execution.environment: macOS local; ESP-IDF v5.5.4 source tree (local); no ESP32-C5 hardware; Device Service 36 profiles and no C5; esp-emulator QEMU has no LP I2C controller / LP IO pad model; no Arduino or PlatformIO build chain installed

checks.detail: init() borrows the pads on every LP port init before i2c_stop() (common.inl:2311-2322); not gated on initialized/handle, so stale LP routing from a previous run is covered
i2c_periph_reset at :1928, pin_backup restore at :1930, lp_pads_return at :1931-1933 - controller reset happens before the pads go back

lp_pads_return (:1857-1881) uses the same elements as IDF v5.5.4 s_lp_i2c_pins_config(): rtc_gpio_init, INPUT_OUTPUT_OD, pulldown_dis, pullup_en, latch high, iomux/connect; SCL clock enabled first and SDA function connected last
IDF v5.5.4 rtc_gpio_init() only enables the per-pin LP IO clock and selects RTCIO_LL_FUNC_RTC; it does not touch direction/pull/latch, so a high latch survives rtc_gpio_init(sda)
i2c_periph_signal[LP port] is in range: C5 static_assert(SOC_I2C_NUM == HP + LP) with iomux_func; C6 second entry; P4 third entry with LP_I2C_*_PAD_*_IDX (IDF v5.5.4 and v5.4.2)
init() opens the LP bus with enable_internal_pullup = true (:2352), so the unconditional rtc_gpio_pullup_en() in lp_pads_return matches
all 26 checks pass: IDF 5.5.2 c5, 5.4.3 c6/p4, 5.4.3/6.0.2 esp32/s3, pioarduino c5 3.3.0 / c6 3.1.3 / p4 3.1.3, translation unit consistency (build only)
deliberate wedged-bus recovery (SDA held low, 9 clocks + STOP, no false START on return) not tested; PR body also lists it as unverified
no ESP32-C5 hardware; ToughC5 / Nesso N1 / Tab5 UnitNFC campaigns not reproduced; author's table quoted only
no C5 profile; C6/P4 QEMU backends model no LP I2C controller and no LP IO MUX / RTC IO pad routing; the observable is pad routing in the LP IO domain, which a GPIO-level model cannot reproduce
IDF 5.4 / 6.0 hardware and IDF 6.1 C5 hardware untested (author also lists them as unverified)

notes: PR left OPEN; one Japanese comment posted; no close, no push to the upstream repository, no code changes to m5stack/M5GFX.
The change matches what was suggested in #426 (borrow the pads, return them in the IDF order, reset the controller first, cover the pre-initialized path).
Only optional suggestion: the LP GPIO matrix branch is gated on SOC_LP_GPIO_MATRIX_SUPPORTED alone while the include also checks __has_include(<driver/lp_io.h>).
Author's hardware table (0/0 -> 100/100 on C5 / C6 / P4, Tab5 first probe 8/8) is quoted, not reproduced here.
